claims.text: Pre-coating AlCrFeNiSi powder with a sub-micron Y2O3 dispersion and using low-thermal-input L-PBF will reduce residual stresses relative to conventional high-thermal-load processing.
The combined nanoparticle and low-thermal-input intervention will improve mechanical properties relative to conventional processing.
Oxide nanoparticles will promote heterogeneous nucleation in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Nanoparticle-promoted heterogeneous nucleation will refine and homogenize the AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
Resonant acoustic mixing can uniformly disperse Y2O3 nanoparticles over the AlCrFeNiSi powder.
Lowering laser power while increasing scanning speed provides a low-thermal-input L-PBF regime for this feedstock.
The intervention is applicable to miniature components smaller than 1 cm.
An argon atmosphere and a layer thickness of approximately 20–40 µm constitute an applicable processing window.
Laser power can be reduced by approximately 25–40% relative to conventional settings while tailored hatch spacing maintains sufficient melt-pool overlap.
Nanoscale oxide precipitates formed during processing act as heterogeneous nucleation sites.
The oxide dispersion enhances thermal conductivity.
Enhanced thermal conductivity from the oxide dispersion mitigates steep thermal gradients.
Oxide nanoparticles lower the energy barrier for nucleation during solidification.
Grain refinement reduces the buildup of residual thermal stresses.
A refined or heterogeneous microstructure can increase strength while retaining deformability.
Lower thermal input simplifies process control by minimizing high thermal gradients.
Modified components will have finer and more uniform grains than conventionally processed components.
Modified components will have higher yield strength while maintaining ductility.
Conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi typically produces high residual stresses and degraded mechanical properties.
Results may not generalize to larger geometries or processing conditions outside the proposed window.
